scenario: Greeting someone for the first time
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hello! My name is Ana.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Hi, Ana. Nice to meet you. I am Carlos.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Nice to meet you too. This is my friend, Luis.
dialogue.translation: Ngiyavuya ukukwazi nalo. Lolu ngumngane wami, Luis.

dialogue.speaker: C
dialogue.text: Hello, Luis. I am from Spain.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: And I am from Mexico. Welcome!

scenario: Asking where something is in a store
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Isigcawu esisetshenziswa ukukhuluma ngento eyakhulunywa ngaphambili.
Into ebekwa khona izinto, ingaba yisikhungo.
Ekhishinini, kutsho ukuthola noma ukufinyelela into.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Excuse me, where is the bread?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It is over there, on that shelf.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is it right there?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes. You need to get it from the top.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Thank you!

scenario: Ordering a drink at a café
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Seyithi ukukhombisa into ngendlela ehloniphekileyo: 'Can I have...?'

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: What can I get for you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Can I have a coffee, please?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hot or cold?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Hot, please. And what tea do you have?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Here you go. Your coffee and tea.

key_phrases.phrase: What can I get for you?

scenario: Buying a ticket at a station
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I want one ticket to London, please.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: For today, with the train now?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yes, but very early, and then I go to work.
dialogue.translation: Yebo, kodwa kakhulu kusasa, futhi ngese ngiyahamba emsebenzini.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: OK, you have the train at six. That is good.
dialogue.translation: Kulungile, unetreni ngamashumi amahlanu. Lokho kulungile.

scenario: Checking in at a hotel reception
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Seyenziwa ukudonsa ukubeka okuthile noma ukudinga okuthile.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Good evening. Do you have a reservation?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, we have a room for two nights.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Here is your key. Your room is on the third floor.
dialogue.translation: Nansi isikhwele sakho. Ikhamera lakho lisesitali esantathu.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Thank you. We need help with our bags.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Of course. How long do you want to stay?

key_phrases.phrase: How long do you want to stay?

scenario: Meeting a new neighbor
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Kulesi sihcoko, 'move' kutsho ukushintsha indawo yokuhlala.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hi! I see you just moved into the house next door.
dialogue.translation: Molo! Ngibona ukuthi uqale uhlala endlini eliseduze.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, I live here now. It is my new home.
dialogue.translation: Yebo, ngihlala lapha manje. Yindlu yami entsha.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That is great! So, do you need help with your things today?
dialogue.translation: Lokhu kuhle kakhulu! Ngakho-ke, uyadinga usizo ngezinto zakho namhlanje?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Maybe later. Oh, the door is open. Let me close it.
dialogue.translation: Mhlawumbe kamuva. Oh, isango livulekile. Ngiyekele ngisivale.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No problem. I am at home all morning. Come by any time.
dialogue.translation: Akukho problema. Ngisendlini yonke ikusasa. Ungaze ungafika nakhathesi.

scenario: Asking the time on the street
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Isethwa ukubuza isikhathi: 'What time is it?'
Kulesi sihcoko, 'Do you have the time?' = Ingabe unesikhathi?
Isethwa ukubonisa ukuphinda noma isikhathi eside.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Excuse me, do you have the time?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sorry, I don't know. I don't have a watch.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Oh, but can you tell me if it's late?
dialogue.translation: Oh, kodwa ungangitshelani ukuthi kulesikhathi eside?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I think it's about three now.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Thank you! See you at three then.

scenario: At the doctor for a basic checkup
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Kusetshenziswa ukukhuluma ngendlela oyiyo ngayo ngokomzimba.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How do you feel today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Not better than yesterday. I have some pain here.
dialogue.translation: Akukho kunani kunokuba kanye. Ninesizathu esithile lapha.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You should take this medicine. All is fine, but rest more.
dialogue.translation: Kufanele uthathe le madi. Konke kulungile, kepha phumula kabanzi.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: How much do I take each day?

scenario: Paying at a supermarket checkout
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That is the total. The price is twenty dollars.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: OK. How much does it cost? Can I pay with a card?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yes, here is the card machine. And here is your receipt.
dialogue.translation: Yebo, lapha ikhinini lekhadi. Nalapha isiboniso sakho.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Thank you. I am out of cash, so card is good.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Here is your change. Have a nice day!

scenario: Calling a friend to make simple plans
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Isikhathi esimodali sokwenza noma ukuba nakho.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hi, this is me. Can you call me today?
dialogue.translation: Sawubona, ngingu mina. Ingabe ungabiza mina lamuhla?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, I can call you now. Where are you?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I am at home. Can you see me tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, I can see you tomorrow. Where do we meet?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Meet me on this street, near the park.
dialogue.translation: Ngihlangene ngaphakathi kwale ndlela, eduze neparaki.

scenario: Describing your family to someone
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Iseshiwo esisebenzisa ukukhuluma ngabantu abahlala kwindlu noma abangokwesiko.
Iseshiwo esisebenzisa ukukhuluma ngokuzadalwa, kungakhulumi ngokuba yingane elikhulu noma elincane.
Iseshiwo esisebenzisa ukukhuluma ngokuzadalwa, kungakhulumi ngokuba yingane elikhulu noma elincane.
Isiqondiso sokubamba noma ukuba noma yini.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tell me about your family.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I live with my mother, father, and two sisters. My brother is not at home.
dialogue.translation: Ngihlala nomama, ubaba, nangabazalwane ababili. Umfowethu akasikhona ekhaya.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is your father old or young?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: He is not very old, but my mother is very young.
dialogue.translation: Akudali kakhulu, kodwa umama encane kakhulu.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: And your sisters? Are they young too?

key_phrases.phrase: live with my mother and father

scenario: Asking for directions in the street
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Excuse me, is the station far from here?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, it's near. Go straight and turn left at the next street.
dialogue.translation: Hayi, iphedeni. Hamba phambili ubuke ngenkululeko kwisitiriti esilandelayo.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Go straight and turn left? Is that right?
dialogue.translation: Hamba phambili ubuke ngenkululeko? Ingabe liyekunene?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, that's right. Then go straight again. The station is on your right.
dialogue.translation: Yebo, liyekunene. Khona-ke, hamba phambili futhi. Isitesheni isekunene kwakho.

scenario: On a bus asking the driver for help
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Excuse me, can you help me? I need to get off at the next stop.
dialogue.translation: Uxolo, ungangisiza? Idinga ukuphuma esikhaleni esilandelayo.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sure. Which stop do you want? This is the next stop.
dialogue.translation: Yebo. Ufuna isikhala sini? Lesi siyisikhala esilandelayo.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I want the stop near the hospital. How many stops from here?
dialogue.translation: Ngifuna isikhala esiseduze nehospitale. Yini izingxenye ezihlukahlukene lapha?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's three stops down. Please sit down, I will tell you.
dialogue.translation: Kuyizingxenye ezintathu phansi. Ngiyabonga uhlale phansi, ngizakutshela.

key_phrases.phrase: get off at the next stop

scenario: Introducing a colleague at work
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Isethulwa esithi indawo nomsebenzi owenziwa emsebenzini.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hello, this is our new colleague. Her name is Ana.
dialogue.translation: Sawubona, lo uyisikolwa esisha. Igama lakhe nguAna.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Nice to meet you, Ana. What do you do here?

dialogue.speaker: C
dialogue.text: She works in our team. He is her manager.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Good! I want to work with you.

scenario: Leaving a voicemail message
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hello, this is Ana. Please leave a message after the beep.
dialogue.translation: Sawubona, ngingu-Ana. Sicela ushiye umyalezo emva kwesibhambathiso.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Hi Ana, this is Luis. Please call me back soon.
dialogue.translation: Molo Ana, ngingu-Luis. Sicela ungikhombise buyela ngesikhathi eside.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Okay, Luis. What is your number?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It is 555-1234. Thank you!

scenario: At the post office sending a package
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Kulesi sihcoko, 'have' siyathusa njengesisekelo esisebenzisayo esikhathini esihle

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I want to send this package to my friend.
dialogue.translation: Ngifisa ukuthumela iphepha le kuze kwabangane bam.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: We have it at the counter. Please fill out this form for the package.
dialogue.translation: Sinayo ku-counter. Nceda uyiqede le forma kuye iphepha.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is this all for the package?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, we have all we need. You can send it now.
dialogue.translation: Yebo, sinayo konke esiyikutholelwa. Ungathumela manje.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Thank you.

scenario: Describing your daily routine
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Isikhathi esikuliswa ngosuku kuvela ngo-6 uya ku-12.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I get up at seven in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Then I have breakfast and go to work.
dialogue.translation: Ngansukela ngidlala ukudla kwenkuseni ngiye esikolweni.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I work at home in the evening.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I watch TV because I like it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Then I sleep at ten.

scenario: Asking about opening hours
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Isetshenziswa ukucaza indawo efanelekile ukusetshenziswa abantu.
Ichiqisa isenzo sokuvala, lapha isetshenziswa ngesikhathi esihambisana.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can you tell me the open time today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: We open at nine, but we close at five.
dialogue.translation: Sivula ngakhamba kakhulu, kodwa sivala ngakhamba amahlanu.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: And on Saturday, until what time are you open?
dialogue.translation: Kanti ngeSonto, kuze kube yini lesikhathi nivule?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: On Saturday, we close at one.

scenario: Choosing a dish from a menu
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: What do you like to eat?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I like fish or chicken with rice.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The fish is very good here.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Then I try some fish, please.

key_phrases.phrase: What do you like to eat?
The fish is very good here.

scenario: At the bank for a simple transaction
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Isitshalo esingasabalwa ngesiNgisi: 'money' asinayo isihloko esiningi.
Mhlaye yisiboniso ('more money') noma isazisi ('more quickly').

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I need money now.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Here is your card. Go there with your ID.
dialogue.translation: Lapha ikhadi lakho. Hamba khona no-ID yakho.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Will you give me more cash?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, I will give you the money now. Go there.
dialogue.translation: Yebo, ngizokunika imali manje. Hamba khona.
